question: Can a seeded return fault actually be injected into the same launch-derived plant, then handled by real Jev and optional DeepSeek through observed symptoms, requested tracking, independent Rules and one-use execution?
selection: sha256(unified-return-trouble-v1:seed), first 8 bytes modulo 2; one draw before any flight; no resampling
probabilities: uniform fault-only test distribution; not historical incident probabilities
stages: one same-case live-sensor full flight after fixture verification
provider_policy: Jev first; DeepSeek only after explicit Jev delegation, within existing 35/150 second decision windows

phase_scope.visual_observation: real pixels and HTTP, fixed response

acceptance: one hash-bound TroubleEngine receipt at accepted dispatch
actual actuator limits or measurement gain agree with the private sampled manifest
no private seed, schedule or fault label in model requests
same physical state and retained mass from launch
live tracking request and final admitted action, with no fallback substituted as an AI choice
independent guard and observed contact limits pass
stop: first invalid evidence or unexpected fixture failure
model failure retained without retry; a checked fallback may protect the flight but cannot satisfy AI-work acceptance
qualification: experimental same-model discrete predictions only; nominal 39-case certificate unchanged
publication: internal PR only; compact reviewed receipts in Git, raw frames and flight records in private durable output, archive and verify before any cleanup
